learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to recognize the relationship between load, deformation, and stress of a component.
They can set up and solve model equations for one-dimensional and simple multi-dimensional structures.
They master the safe and economical design of components and structures.

syllabus_topics: Tension and compression in bars, single bar, statically determinate and indeterminate bar systems
Two- and three-dimensional stress state, stress vector, stress transformation, principal stresses, Mohr's stress circle, thin-walled vessels, equilibrium conditions
Deformation and strain state, transformation of strains
Relationship between stresses and strains (Hooke's Law, one-dimensional, multi-dimensional, thermal expansion), strength hypotheses
Beam bending, area moments of inertia, pure bending (shear-rigid), normal stresses, deflection curve (beams with one and several fields), influence of shear, bending and tension/compression
Torsion, circular cylindrical shaft, thin-walled closed and open profiles
Concept of work, work theorem for statically determinate and indeterminate systems (PdvV and PdvK)
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The examination format (written exam or project/presentation with short questions) will be announced and explained at the beginning of the lecture.
